WELCOME TO MATICIAN’S SPACE

You don’t need to know
where to start.

A lab is a small, interactive maths experiment. You can explore every tool without an account. Start with an example; there’s no need to fill in every setting.

  1. 1
    Pick something you’re curious about.

    Use Home to browse topics, or Search to find a lab by words like “slope” or “area”.

  2. 2
    Load an easy example.

    Each lab has a starting example. Change a value, then select Calculate or Update results. Sliders update automatically.

  3. 3
    Look for what changed.

    Read the short explanation above the results. Use “Explain this lab” for useful words and “Advanced settings” when you want more control.

Nothing to break. Reset restores a lab’s original example. On a phone, “See your results” takes you straight to the answer.

How calculations work & what to keep in mind

A real local maths engine

JavaScript algorithms and bundled Mathjs symbolic rules compute locally. No server, account or network connection is needed.

Verification, not a promise

Executable checks compare methods to known answers. They are targeted regression tests, not proof for every possible input.

Every approximation has a limit.

Derivative rules have real-domain conditions. Root searches and contours are sampled, not exhaustive proofs. ODE solvers use fixed steps. Fractals use finite iterations and float64. Chaotic trajectories depend on both initial values and numerical error. A small residual does not always mean a small solution error.

Symbolic differentiation uses SymPy in the Python edition and locally bundled Mathjs 15.2.0 in the browser edition. Standard-rule domain exclusions are conservative; a limit may still exist at an excluded chain-rule point.

New ways to explore. The Graphing notebook plots multiple functions with sliders, pan/zoom, tracing and tables. Prime numbers now includes large-number tests, formula lessons, an exact Mersenne lab, and a dated record card. A probable prime is not a primality proof.
